campaign.topic: S1-003 execute real SHACL engine and close semantic evidence provenance

claims.text: Fact: requirements-pyshacl.txt is a single --require-hashes lock for rdflib 7.6.0, pySHACL 0.40.1, owlrl 7.6.2, and ALL transitive deps (pyparsing 3.3.2, html5rdf 1.2.1, packaging 26.3, prettytable 3.18.0, wcwidth 0.8.2, importlib_metadata 9.0.0, zipp 4.1.0). Hashes captured from real PyPI wheels.
Schema fact: all 13 expected lifecycle states were represented, with 13 valid fixtures, 11 invalid fixtures, and five ownership/scope failure fixtures.

Fact: structural oracle and pySHACL engine (shapes-v3.ttl, which preserves all original v1 constraints) agree on 26/26 profile runs — 24 open + 2 promoted_only, 13 valid + 11 invalid, 13/13 lifecycle states.

Fact: pySHACL v0.40.1 executed against shapes-v3.ttl (which preserves ALL original v1 property constraints including sh:maxCount=1, sh:node, sh:class, and sh:or) over 24 fixtures and 26 profile runs, matching the structural oracle on all 26 (conforms + intended primary reason).

Constraint: the shapes contain sh:maxInclusive and rejected, contain no forbidden tokens (maxExclusiveInclusive-class, accepted/withdrawn status literals, sh:closed true), and the stale accepted fixture is rejected by both structural oracle and pySHACL engine. shapes-v3.ttl preserves all original v1 constraints including sh:maxExclusiveInclusive absence.

Constraint: a promoted assertion requires exactly one PromotionActivity, at least two evidence records, at least two distinct canonical_source_id values, at least two independence_group values, complete resolver provenance, and matching workspace scope.

Design inference: SQL constraints and application validators remain canonical enforcement for the MVP while SHACL is a portable projection and conformance contract, so runtime absence does not authorize weaker promotion semantics.

Tool availability limit: rdflib and pyshacl were not importable in the execution environment and pySHACL was not executed; Turtle parsing, RDF entailment, SHACL-engine conformance, and SHACL-SPARQL behavior remain unverified.

Inference: shapes-v3.ttl preserves the original constraints and a fresh engine-schema-v2 replay produced canonical semantic tuples whose digests, exact violation sets, per-run outcomes, complete generator/input hashes, coverage, summary, and verdict were independently recomputed by the fail-closed comparator. With 26/26 agreement, 42 regression tests, and 12/12 adversarial probes, the S1-003 verdict is PASS. The original PASS_WITH_LIMITS remains preserved and superseded in audit.history.

Inference: with pySHACL engine execution producing 26/26 agreement and all adversarial probes passing, the S1-003 ticket verdict is promoted from PASS_WITH_LIMITS to PASS. The original PASS_WITH_LIMITS evidence is preserved in audit.history.

Fact: all 12/12 mandatory adversarial probe checks executed via real pySHACL engine passed, confirming open-shape tolerance, promotion grounding, mirror/Sybil rejection, independence group enforcement, scope isolation, supersession, stale-vocabulary rejection, and forbidden-token absence.

Near miss: proposed with inherited ContentObject extras passes the open structural profile but fails promoted_only; orphan promotion, mirror-source promotion, and missing independence group each fail for the intended reason.

Run the frozen shapes and equivalent RDF fixtures through a pinned pySHACL version, record the version and report graph, and promote S1-003 from PASS_WITH_LIMITS only if all expected outcomes remain identical.
Schema fact: the bounded stdlib validator executed 26 profile checks over 24 fixtures and matched every declared expected outcome and intended primary failure reason.

Design inference: the ontology contract is ready as a versioned structural baseline for S1-004 and S1-011, but not as a fully engine-validated SHACL release; the correct ticket verdict is PASS_WITH_LIMITS.

Schema fact: the audited contract contains seven KnowledgeAssertion states, six DelegationGrant states, open shapes, conditional promotion evidence, EvidenceShape provenance fields, maxInclusive TTL, and non-negative budget.
The structural run does not prove that shapes.ttl parses in an RDF engine or that its SHACL-SPARQL query behaves identically across conforming implementations.

Fact: comparison.py is fail-closed — every expectation and canonical semantic tuple is derived exclusively from raw-results.json, while every input/generator hash is recomputed from disk. Schema, exact result keys, runtime pins, complete run coverage, exact sorted violation strings, semantic tuples and their derived digest, strict booleans, per-run matched consistency, summary, coverage, verdict, and mismatch fields must all agree. Verdict is pass only for exactly 26 independently matched runs with zero mismatches. 42 adversarial regression tests cover the evidence, schema, provenance, workspace-root, and bounded-memory hashing paths.
Fact: fixtures_to_rdf.py emits inherited_content_object_properties on the assertion root (not only on supportedBy evidence), ensuring all 24 fixtures have complete RDF projections.

Constraint: shapes-v3.ttl preserves ALL original v1 property constraints — sh:maxCount=1 on prov:wasGeneratedBy (promotion), sh:node hubs:EvidenceShape on supportedBy, sh:maxCount=1 + sh:class hubs:KnowledgeAssertion on supersededBy, sh:minCount=2 on supportedBy. New SPARQL checks for distinct canonical sources, independence groups, and scope mismatches are ADDED on top.
